hypothesis: For the same connected radial topology and vertex budget, uniformly spaced rings shaped after the full height is established will approximate a smooth target profile more accurately and with more even quad density than manually accumulated uneven extrude-and-scale steps.
negative_control: One connected 12-sided mesh with 13 deliberately uneven ring heights and small deterministic per-step radius errors, representing accumulated manual step-extrusion imprecision.
candidate: One connected 12-sided mesh with 13 uniformly spaced rings whose radii are sampled from the same declared target profile after the full height is established.
claim_boundary: The control deliberately contains uneven spacing and small manual radius errors; this tests the tutorial's demonstrated failure mode, not a universal claim that every manually stepped mesh must be inferior. A pass validates this principle for one different radial product form only.
